search_bias: Autonomous-scientist systems and empirical research-agent papers; citation-chain from strongest quantitative primary sources. This run prioritized same-model or same-harness comparisons, component ablations, executable scientific artifacts, and failure-recovery mechanisms. It resumed only the clean_g1 scientist_agents checkpoint, then followed the AIRS/ASI/verification frontier into SAGE, EviGraph, AI Scientist compute-scaling evidence, and a physical chemistry protocol-compilation system (ACRA).

evidence_updates.update: AIRS same-model Greedy-vs-One-Shot comparisons strengthen the scaffold signal while avoiding much of the cross-model confound: gpt-oss-120b 0.402 vs 0.161 (+0.241), gpt-oss-20b 0.400 vs 0.077 (+0.323), o3-mini 0.391 vs 0.171 (+0.220), GPT-4o 0.309 vs 0.057 (+0.252), CWM 0.287 vs 0.041 (+0.246), Devstral 0.179 vs 0.018 (+0.161) on the leaderboard's average normalized score. Greedy-vs-ReAct remains less cleanly causal because AIRA-dojo and MLGym impose different per-solution limits, data splits, and test-scoring semantics; with CWM, ReAct 0.302 slightly exceeds Greedy 0.287, while with GPT-4o Greedy 0.309 exceeds ReAct 0.178. Preserve scaffold/harness interaction rather than universal tree-search superiority.

Within the peer-reviewed AI Scientist workflow, increasing experimental-node budget from 5 to 32 raised automated-review paper score from 3.30 to 3.93 (n=30 at each budget; intermediate 8=3.35, 16=3.40). This supports deeper within-workflow search, but the outcome is an automated reviewer score and does not isolate tree topology from extra compute.

ACRA provides a concrete domain-specific instance of procedure compilation: natural-language synthesis procedures are decomposed into an executable symbolic XDL, checked syntactically, compared back against the source procedure by a critique agent, mapped onto hardware, simulated under physical constraints, then optionally executed on robots. This is faithful-reproduction evidence, not evidence of open-ended novel method invention.

SAGE supplies a prospective intervention rather than only post-hoc failure taxonomy: structured multi-hypothesis failure diagnosis plus independent criticism and hierarchy-aware routing materially outperforms a same-harness free-form-reflection baseline. Its numeric-grounding layer also reveals a boundary: number-level provenance is insufficient for prose-level method/library/dataset provenance, so plan-execution-evidence consistency must extend beyond numeric tables.

Compute evidence is now explicitly two-sided: AI Scientist shows within-workflow node scaling 3.30->3.93 from 5->32 experimental nodes, while prior MLReplicate cross-system evidence shows resource use is not a reliable ordering of human scientific quality. Treat workflow architecture and compute budget as separate axes and demand matched scaling curves.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Multi-hypothesis failure attribution with independent causal criticism and hierarchy-aware repair routing: preserve several evidence-grounded explanations for a failed experiment, score/support-check them independently, then deterministically route the verified cause to hypothesis-, design-, or implementation-level repair rather than performing one monolithic reflection.
evidence: SAGE evaluates a 12-topic, five-domain ARC-Bench subset and compares against a same-harness SAGE-without-MHFA reflection baseline, keeping the surrounding workflow substantially fixed.
Metric-bearing recovery rises from 5/12 (42%) under reflection to 11/12 (92%) with SAGE; calibrated AR-Eval rises from 5.00 to 6.75/10.
Blind human PhD review on the ML subset scores SAGE 5.67/10 versus the reflection baseline 3.00; SAGE also outscores AI Scientist-v2 in the reported uniform artifact evaluation, 52.0 vs 48.2.

Reported component ablations degrade the score range when the independent critic, divergent hypothesis generation, or MHFA are removed; removing MHFA is the largest stated degradation, making this materially stronger evidence than an architecture-only package comparison.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Twelve benchmark topics across five domains; human review covers six ML topics. Strong evidence for structured failure recovery in this harness, not proof of general scientific discovery or conference-ready manuscript quality.
candidate_mechanisms_new.uncertainty: Need replication across independent harnesses/models and matched cost/runtime accounting. Need to test whether benefits persist when failures are ambiguous, multiple causes are jointly active, or critic errors are correlated with generator errors.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Typed evidence-dependency graph as operational research state, with earliest-weak-node localization, transactional downstream regeneration, checkpoint/rollback, and a manuscript-readiness gate that requires every retained claim to have a validated evidence chain.
evidence: EviGraph explicitly represents Problem, Gap, Hypothesis, Experiment, Finding, and Claim nodes and checks evidence chains for missing dependencies, semantic misalignment, and result-claim inconsistency.

On ARC-Bench-ML, the paper reports overall research performance 86.45% for EviGraph versus about 60.37% for the strongest compared baseline in the reported table; Claim Support Rate is 37.85% versus 27% (+40.19% relative).

Experimental Data Consistency reaches 87.73%; this is not universally best because another compared system reports 96.15% EDC, so EviGraph's advantage should be framed as joint evidence-state performance rather than dominance on every metric.

The published abstract reports strong end-to-end gains but no clean component-level ablation was found in this run, so causal credit cannot yet be assigned separately to graph representation, weak-node localization, rollback, or repair memory.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: ARC-Bench-ML and NanoResearch-20 system-level results. Package-level evidence only until component ablations, repeated seeds, judge calibration, and budget accounting are extracted.
candidate_mechanisms_new.uncertainty: Need primary-table/appendix verification of baselines, seeds, confidence intervals, token/tool budgets, judge dependence, and rollback/memory-specific ablations.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Executable scientific intermediate representation plus layered verification: compile natural-language experimental procedures into a domain DSL, validate syntax and source-procedure fidelity, simulate against actual hardware constraints, then execute physically only after those gates pass; retain validated examples as retrieval memory.
evidence: ACRA translates literature chemistry into XDL, applies parser feedback, an LLM critique for missing/disordered steps, hardware-constrained simulation, and then execution on Chemputer or Opentrons-OT2 systems; six realistic syntheses were directly executed from literature on two robotic platforms.

Across 150 randomly sampled ChemRnD procedures (three independent samples of 50), 99.33% reached syntactically valid XDL and 94.67% passed the subsequent source-discrepancy and hardware-simulation validation stages, with at most six generate-validate-repair iterations.

Memory/data ablation on 75 procedures shows overall late-stage validation success rising from 85.3% with all external databases/data removed to 93.3% with the full memory/data stack. With a seeded XDL database, 6.7% failed late validation; with no initial XDL database or no XDL database, 9.3% and 10.7% failed respectively.

The paper explicitly warns that executability checks do not guarantee completeness or accuracy, and shows that syntax alone is insufficient; a critique step and hardware simulation catch missing/disordered steps and physically invalid parameters.
Two tested open-source models up to 70B failed to generate valid XDL in this setup, so the mechanism's observed performance is model-dependent.

The system collected 350 unsupported steps and clustered them into 26 candidate XDL feature additions, suggesting a concrete route for the executable representation itself to evolve from observed capability gaps.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Faithful reproduction/verification of published synthetic-chemistry procedures, not open-ended novel scientific discovery. The strongest quantitative evidence concerns translation and executability, not discovery quality.
candidate_mechanisms_new.uncertainty: Need judge-free/manual fidelity metrics for the critique stage, explicit no-critique numeric ablation values, cost/runtime, and tests in domains where procedure semantics cannot be captured by a mature symbolic DSL.

negative_and_boundary_evidence_new: SAGE's large gains in metrics-bearing recovery and artifact quality do not make conference-ready scientific papers: the work itself states fully autonomous scientific writing remains difficult, and prior detailed evaluation reports strict paper-only scores remaining low. Keep recovery quality separate from publication validity.
EviGraph's Claim Support Rate of 37.85% is substantially better than the compared strongest baseline but still low in absolute terms; explicit evidence graphs do not eliminate unsupported claims.

ACRA's layered verification separates syntax from scientific/procedural fidelity: even when nearly all outputs are valid XDL, later discrepancy/simulation stages still reject a material fraction. Executable syntax is not evidence of complete scientific correctness.
ACRA's two tested open-source models up to 70B failed to generate valid XDL, showing that workflow structure does not erase base-model capability dependence.

AIRS Greedy-vs-ReAct comparisons are not fully controlled because their harnesses differ in per-solution time limits, cross-validation/data split policy, and which solutions are test-scored. Do not infer universal search-topology causality from those cross-harness pairs.
The AI Scientist node-scaling result uses an automated reviewer score; deeper search improving that score is not equivalent to independently validated scientific truth.

termination_diagnostics.additional_unresolved_frontier_action_be: After the run already had reportable SAGE/EviGraph/AIRS/Nature updates, it deliberately followed the unresolved procedure-compilation frontier into the peer-reviewed ACRA chemputation paper. It extracted the 150-procedure layered-validation result (99.33% syntactic validity, 94.67% late-stage validation), the 75-procedure memory/data ablation (85.3%->93.3%), six physical literature-to-robot synthesis examples across two platforms, open-model failure, and unsupported-step roadmap evidence.
termination_diagnostics.worker_behavior_correction: No finding, summary readiness, or single-source completion was treated as terminal. Cross-harness comparisons were explicitly demoted when controls differed; package-level results were not promoted to component causality without ablation.
termination_diagnostics.stop_reason: Scheduled-run checkpoint with a nonempty empirical frontier; research remains open.

exact_next_action: Extract EviGraph's primary tables/appendix for causal-component and judge/budget details, then quantify ACRA's critique-agent no-judge ablation; after that finish MLReplicate's full system-by-system resource/human-evaluation table and compare SAGE MHFA against repeated free-form reflection under matched compute.
